reason: The cited evidence supports that sigma phase particles pin dislocations and grain boundaries, and that Mo addition enhances this effect. However, it provides no direct evidence that W or Ta additions promote sigma phase formation or dispersion in refractory high-entropy alloys, nor that such dispersion improves high-temperature ductility or creep life at ~650°C. The key premise that W/Ta acts analogously to Mo is an unsupported extrapolation.
premises: Sigma phase particles pin dislocations and grain boundaries, refining microstructure and improving strength.
Adding Mo enhances sigma phase volume fraction, stability, and pinning effect.
Adding W or Ta will similarly promote sigma phase formation and dispersion.
Uniformly dispersed sigma phase particles improve high-temperature ductility and creep life.
The mechanism operates effectively at ~650°C in refractory high-entropy alloys.
